correctness.rationale: The full projective product P3_[x:y:z:w]×P2_[s:u:v] over C is used; with A=xw, B=yz, D=A-B the claimed quartic is precisely F=A²(u-v)²−2AB(s(u+v)+u²+v²)+B²(s+u+v)². Its quadratic matrix in (s,u,v) has determinant −4A²B²(A−B)², so the smooth-conic case ABD!=0 is nonsingular. On A=0, B=0, D=0, the restricted first derivatives and chain rule identify exactly four 3D coordinate-line×P2 loci and twelve additional irreducible 2D surfaces; at A=B=0 all first derivatives vanish. Each surface has points off the others, proving irreducible components rather than just candidates. Transverse Hessians of the five surface symmetry types have rank three on a dense open, giving A1 ordinary quadratic nodes, while the discriminant of the normal quadratic in (A,B) is 16uv(s+u)(s+v) generically nonzero on the 3D loci, giving normal crossings. As the hypersurface is irreducible and has codimension-one singular divisors, R1 fails and it is nonnormal (no claim about Jacobian nilpotents or intersection analytic types). Independent symbolic algebra confirms polynomial identity, Q determinant and normal discriminant; these computations support but do not replace the algebraic saturation-by-cases proof.
